free_tier.stated: At SourceForge.net, each project is provided the PROJECT.sourceforge.io subdomain, where “PROJECT” is your project’s UNIX name.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: The Project Web documentation lists SFTP, SCP and rsync uploads and states no per-object size cap.

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: The Project Web documentation calls the service always-on and gives no expiry or retention interval for uploaded files.

egress.terms: 'Unlimited bandwidth for Open Source projects' (sourceforge.net/create). 'Our project web servers frequently handle more than 50M hits per day; we handle server scaling, caching, load balancing, and performance tuning.' Served through Cloudflare.

tooling: Same SFTP/SCP/rsync upload path as FRS but to /home/project-web/<unixname>/htdocs. Static files come back over plain HTTPS on <unixname>.sourceforge.io. No client, no API, just a web origin. Custom domains supported via the Custom VHOST service.
chaining: Each project is allocated a UNIXNAME.sourceforge.io virtual host to serve its project web content.
limits_note: Per-object-cap: none published (it is a web root, not an artefact store). Request-rate: none published. Retention: 'always-on' service, files persist while the project exists. Practical caveat: it is a *web* root. Directory indexes are not guaranteed, so you index your own paths.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Probed live: https://libreoffice.sourceforge.io/ -> 200 with 134,123 bytes of real HTML; https://gimp.sourceforge.io/ -> 403 (project redirects elsewhere). https://gparted.sourceforge.io/ -> 302 to the project's own domain. Expect some projects to 403/302 depending on their custom-VHOST config; a fresh project should serve its own root.

extras.egress_verbatim: 'Unlimited bandwidth for Open Source projects' (sourceforge.net/create). 'Our project web servers frequently handle more than 50M hits per day; we handle server scaling, caching, load balancing, and performance tuning.' Served through Cloudflare.
extras.chaining_verbatim: A second independent quota-less origin per project, free once you already have the project. Because it is a static web origin rather than a download mirror, it is the natural Cloudflare-fronted serving layer for anything in FRS: serves as the hot/serving tier while FRS holds the archive. N projects -> N vhosts.

extras.agent_focus: Seedboxes, file-transfer protocols and niche transports with free tiers: free seedbox providers, FTP/SFTP hosts, rsync.net, Borg/restic backends, systematic rclone-backend enumeration, WebDAV providers, free Usenet/NNTP, free VPS with big disk. Transport-first, not drive-first.
